subject: Packaging options: seat-to-throughput conversion & feature orchestration
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@carewell.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@carewell.ai>
Date: Sat, 05 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging options: can we swap seats for throughput?

Hi Karthik,

Quick background: CareWell is expanding our triage and summarization pipelines and we expect token volume to double Q4. Right now we pay per-seat (30 seats) and some add-on entitlements (NER + Compliance filtering). We want to explore two things:

- Whether we can convert some seats into dedicated throughput (reserved capacity) to lower per-token costs while keeping the features we need.
- How feature entitlements (NER/Compliance) move across a seat-first vs throughput-first approach.

We're open to a 12-month commitment if the math works — also curious what kind of discount / credit you'd offer for moving 12 seats to a throughput pool for 1 year. Attached is a short usage extract.

Can you propose options (rough $) and a recommended path for minimal disruption? Also keen to run a short 30-min workshop with your team to map traffic shapes.

Thanks —
Evan
Evan Brooks
Head of Product
CareWell.ai

Attachment: carewell_usage_q3.csv (usage snapshot, rows: 432)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@carewell.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 05 Sep 2026 12:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options: can we swap seats for throughput?

Evan —

Thanks for the context and the usage file. We can absolutely support a seat -> throughput conversion without forcing you to lose feature entitlements. High-level options (quick sketch):

1) Throughput-first (recommended for heavy token growth)
   - Convert 12 seats into a Dedicated Throughput pool (reserved GPU hours) sized for your 2x token growth.
   - Keep feature entitlements (NER, Compliance) on a per-request basis; we'll route requests through the Dedicated pool.
   - Pricing: estimated ~ $X/month for reserved throughput (see attached ratecard). For a 12-month commit, we can offer an "upto 20%" discount on the throughput unit price, plus a one-time migration credit to offset the first month.

2) Seat-first (minimize operational change)
   - Keep seat licenses but apply a credit system (token credits) to approximate the cost benefits of throughput.
   - Feature entitlements remain tied to seats; you retain seat-based admin UX.
   - Pricing: smaller immediate savings, simpler rollout.

Tradeoffs: throughput-first gives lower unit cost at the expense of some changes to UI/seat management; seat-first preserves current controls but reduces upside.

Next steps I suggest:
- I’ll put together a one-pager with concrete numbers for both options (capacity sizing + price table).
- Schedule a 30-min workshop with your infra/MLOps team to confirm traffic distribution and cold-start constraints.

For transparency, I’m looping Lauren (GTMS) and Ben (Revenue Ops) to align on discount levers. Will follow up with a proposal PDF by EOD Monday.

—
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Attachment: karthik_proposal_v1.pdf (sketch — capacity tiers + assumptions)
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@carewell.ai>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@carewell.ai>
Date: Sun, 06 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options: can we swap seats for throughput?

Looping in a couple of quick guardrails from packaging/pricing:

- Historical precedent: for throughput commitments at this size we typically land between 15–18% off list for a 12-month commit (20% is usually reserved for larger multi-year or pilot+commit deals).
- If we keep feature entitlements attached to requests routed via Dedicated, add a small per-request feature surcharge (covering NER model cost) — call it a feature multiplier rather than re-licensing seats.
- Need finance approval for any one-time migration credit. If Karithk puts the proposed numbers into HubSpot, please include the estimated ARR change and the expected start date for the commit.

Karthik — happy to review the one-pager before you send it to Evan.

— Lauren Bishop
Head of GTM Pricing, Redwood Inference

- Throughput discount: approve up to 18% for a 12-month committed throughput pool for CareWell.ai (DW-2026-0182).
- One-time migration credit: approve up to 1 month equivalent as a one-off credit.

Please capture the concession in HubSpot and mark it in the quote as an approved concession so finance sees it up front.
